answer: Neighborhood Persistence Routing. Agents route work only through peers whose local graph shows sustained two-way traffic over many epochs. A newcomer must wander across many unrelated neighborhoods to accumulate that history, and each fabricated identity pays its own full routing-history cost. The topology leaves an opal-like unique trace per cluster, while fake clusters stay yarrow-thin and isolated. Attackers must sustain real traffic across many disjoint regions simultaneously, multiplying cost per sybil linearly.
